_about: How each kind of review item moves the estimate (review.impact, Q6197). An item's impact is the price of the takeoff lines it touches (its elements' share of each line, or what the missing quantity costs priced like the lines of its kind); `low` and `high` are the fractions of that price the estimate may move down or up while the item is unresolved. Estimating practice, editable: a project that knows better changes these numbers, never the code.

missing.why: the documents show work the model doesn't have: when it is real the estimate is short its whole price

extra.why: the model has work the documents don't show: when it is wrong the estimate is over by its price

wrong.why: a size, type, place or connection the documents give otherwise: the right one may cost up to half more or less

unsure.why: nothing says yet (no product data, no schedule row, a check that waits on other work): a quarter either way

conflict.why: two documents disagree: either side's price, up to half apart

assumed.why: a default the model assumed (a height, a mounting): little cost either way

proposed.why: work CADaddy laid out itself: the field route or place is more often longer than shorter

gap.why: an open question to the design team: the answer may add or remove up to half of what it touches

finding.why: something the job could not read or decide: up to half of what it touches either way

question: gap

accept.why: the model and the estimate stand as they are

change.why: the model or the estimate was changed to settle it

rfi_sent.why: asked of the design team: open in the estimate until it is answered

labor_rate_source: bim.estimate's default crew rate (dollars per labor hour), used when estimate.settings has no crew_rate

shown_not_priced.G-CLASH: a clash costs the rework of a route, not the price of the element it runs into (the row names the obstacle)
shown_not_priced.E-CONDUIT-CONTINUITY: a raceway gap costs the missing piece of raceway, not the device the row names

_run_item: what a laid-out run is priced as (through the estimate's prices, the price book, the starter book) when the takeoff has no line of its size
